title: Setup transaction
responsibility: Own one project-wide lock for the whole of setup, and make every lasting write happen under a plan rather than in sequence: canonicalise and print each target before mutating, schema-validate every file it may read or merge, probe same-directory temporary-file creation and atomic rename in each parent it will write to, record the identity of each existing file, re-compare that identity immediately before each merge, and maintain a non-secret journal that names the last completed phase so an interruption resumes rather than restarts.
notes: ⚠️ IT REUSES THE EXISTING LOCK RATHER THAN ADDING ONE. The initializer already owns `<project>/.planning-init.lock`; a second lock beside it would let setup and initialization interleave on the same files while each believed it held the project. The initializer and the ignore owner must therefore accept an already-held transaction instead of acquiring their own. ⚠️ THERE IS NO --force. A malformed file is a refusal, because the only thing --force could mean here is overwriting something the operator wrote and setup could not parse.
